verdict.rationale: Linear's changelog says its cloud coding sessions, where Linear Agent writes code, support signed commits once a user adds an SSH or GPG key in Settings. That covers the core of the story: AI-authored commits signed with the engineer's own key. Missing for 10: evidence that signing can be enforced as a requirement (e.g., blocking unsigned agent commits or a workspace-level policy), in-depth documentation beyond a single changelog line, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can require AI-authored commits to be cryptographically signed with my SSH or GPG key

citations.quote: Coding sessions now support signed commits. Add your SSH or GPG key in Settings to enable signing.
Linear Agent can now write code using Claude Code and Codex.
Coding sessions run in the cloud, so you can prototype ideas and make changes without setting up a local development environment.
